overall: Washington DC is warming briskly this morning, with the current temperature at 80.6°F by 9:50 AM and a positive velocity of +3.6°F/hr — suggesting the day is broadly on track for a hot afternoon. Skies are partly broken (BKN, ~62% cloud fraction) but not obstructing warming meaningfully yet. The day is trending consistent with model expectations for a hot but storm-interrupted afternoon, with NWS flagging scattered thunderstorms developing after 3 PM that could cap or cut short the temperature peak.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models show moderate spread: HRRR is the warmest at 91.8°F, ECMWF near 89.9°F, and NBM the most conservative at 88.5°F, while the official NWS call of 93°F sits above all three. The META model (most reliable fusion) splits mass between 86-87°F and 88-89°F at 30.9% each, more cautious than both NWS and HRRR, likely reflecting the storm-capping risk in the 3-5 PM window that could truncate the warming curve before models' predicted peak near 16:00-17:00 ET.
max_temp_prediction: With ~8-11°F of additional warming needed from the current 80.6°F and the peak timing models pointing to mid-afternoon (14:00-17:00 ET), the high is most likely to land in the 90-92°F range — consistent with the even-bucket top of 90-91°F carrying 62.4% in D1_NOW. The primary downside risk is early storm development curtailing afternoon warming below 90°F, while the upside scenario (reaching NWS's 93°F) requires storms to hold off and a sustained warming pace. Confidence is moderate-good; the 90-91°F even bucket is well-supported by HRRR and ECMWF, though the META model's lean toward 86-89°F warrants watching.
